author: fwyzard
body:
#### PR description:

This PR speeds up the alpaka CA kernels of `RecoTracker/PixelSeeding` on GPUs, mostly by reducing the number of idle threads in the kernels where the work per thread varies a lot from one element to the next.

Technical only, the physics results are unchanged.

The changes, one per commit:
- **Iterative depth-first search in `Kernel_find_ntuplets`**: the recursive `CACell::find_ntuplets` was inlined once per depth (226 registers per thread on CUDA); `find_ntuplets_iterative` does the same visit with an explicit per-thread stack (56 registers).
- **Compact the starting cells of `Kernel_find_ntuplets`**: a new `Kernel_select_starts` collects the cells that can start an ntuplet, so that `Kernel_find_ntuplets` runs only over them.
- **Use 2 threads per cell in `Kernel_connect`** instead of 4.
- **Balance the work of `Kernel_connect` across threads on GPUs**: `Kernel_connectBalanced` takes 128 outer cells per block and spreads the (outer cell, candidate inner cell) pairs evenly over the threads of the block, using a prefix sum in shared memory.
- **Go through the whole phi window at once in `GetDoubletsFromHisto`**: the bins of the phi window of an inner hit are contiguous in the `PhiBinner`, so the threads go through the whole window instead of bin by bin.
- **Balance the light cells of the fast duplicate remover on GPUs**: the (cell, track) pairs of the cells with at most `kDupHeavyMinTracks` tracks are spread over the threads of a block.
- **Search the ntuplets one depth at a time on GPUs**: one launch of `Kernel_find_ntuplets_level` per depth, each thread expanding one node of the search tree; a node that does not fit in the node storage (one node per cell) is searched depth first, so the result does not depend on the storage size.

The balanced `Kernel_connect`, the balanced duplicate remover and the level-by-level search are used only by the back-ends with more than one thread per block; the back-ends with a single thread per block (`alpaka::isSingleThreadAcc`, i.e. the serial and TBB CPU back-ends) keep the previous algorithms. The other changes apply to all back-ends.

Throughput of the Phase-2 NGT tracking (`HLT:75e33_trackingOnly` with `--procModifiers alpaka,ngtScouting`, D128) on the GPU, reading the events with `RepeatingCachedRootSource`, on a pod with 31 cores of a 2 AMD EPYC 9534 machine and one NVIDIA L40S, measured along the commits on `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-24-1100` (average  sigma of 4 measurements, in ev/s; 3 jobs run with NVIDIA MPS):

| | Commit | 1 job  24 cores | 3 jobs  8 cores |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | baseline IB | 192.9  0.2 | 203.8  0.3 |
| 1 | Iterative depth-first search in `Kernel_find_ntuplets` | 200.7  0.3 (+4.0%) | 216.1  0.3 (+6.1%) |
| 2 | Compact the starting cells of `Kernel_find_ntuplets` | 204.3  0.2 (+5.9%) | 217.5  0.5 (+6.7%) |
| 3 | Use 2 threads per cell in `Kernel_connect` | 208.3  0.2 (+8.0%) | 223.5  0.3 (+9.7%) |
| 4 | Balance the work of `Kernel_connect` across threads on GPUs | 226.1  0.2 (+17.2%) | 238.3  0.1 (+16.9%) |
| 5 | Go through the whole phi window at once in `GetDoubletsFromHisto` |  |  |
| 6 | Balance the light cells of the fast duplicate remover on GPUs | 235.4  0.9 (+22.0%) | 247.2  0.3 (+21.3%) |
| 7 | Search the ntuplets one depth at a time on GPUs | 240.0  0.2 (+24.4%) | 250.5  0.4 (+22.9%) |

#### PR validation:

On `CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-25-2300`, with the same setup:
- throughput: 1 job  24 cores 192.2  0.2  239.4  0.1 ev/s (+24.5%), 3 jobs  8 cores 203.0  0.2  249.7  0.3 ev/s (+23.0%);
- physics: over 1000 events, the tracks (`hltGeneralTracks`) and pixel vertices (`hltPhase2PixelVertices`) are identical to those of the IB, both on the GPU (1878301 tracks, 209358 vertices) and with the serial CPU back-end (1878305 tracks, 209359 vertices): same number per event, and identical values of pt, eta, phi, chi2/ndof, number of valid hits, dxy, dz and charge of the tracks, and of the position, ndof, chi2 and number of tracks of the vertices;
- the package builds without warnings, and its unit tests pass.
title: Optimise the CA kernels
